stories.h: US Congress to hold hearing on Nigeria's protection of Christians and the Middle Belt
stories.p: A US House subcommittee chaired by Congressman Chris Smith will hold a hearing on Thursday, 12 November, to assess Nigeria's efforts to protect Christians and curb violence in the Middle Belt, with State Department officials due to testify.
body: A United States congressional committee will hold a hearing this week to review Nigeria's record on protecting Christians and tackling violence in the Middle Belt.
## The hearing

The House Foreign Affairs Africa Subcommittee will hold the session on Thursday, 12 November 2026, according to a notice from the office of its chairman, Republican Congressman Chris Smith of New Jersey, issued on Monday. The hearing is titled 'One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria's Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt'.
## What will be discussed

The hearing will examine religious violence by extremist groups, including Boko Haram, and how effectively the Nigerian government has responded to attacks on vulnerable communities. It will also consider what measures the United States could press for to make sure perpetrators are held accountable and to prevent future attacks on Christians and non-radical Muslims. The first panel will hear from two senior State Department officials, Frank Garcia, assistant secretary of state for African affairs, and Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labour, followed by outside experts.
## Background

The title refers to developments around a year ago, when the US designated Nigeria a 'Country of Particular Concern' over religious freedom. The Nigerian government has rejected claims of a targeted genocide against Christians, saying insecurity affects people of all faiths, and has pointed to military operations against armed groups. Attacks have continued in states such as Plateau and Benue, including a deadly attack in Barkin Ladi at the weekend.
more: The hearing is on Thursday, 12 November.
Two senior State Department officials will testify.
It follows US criticism of Nigeria a year ago.

stories.h: Republican congressman files articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth over Iran war
stories.p: Republican Congressman Thomas Massie has introduced articles of impeachment against US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war against Iran without congressional authorisation, as criticism of the conflict grows after the midterms.
body: Articles of impeachment have been introduced in the US House of Representatives against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
## What happened

Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky brought the resolution on Monday, 9 November 2026, as Congress returned for a 'lame-duck' session after the midterm elections. Massie accused Hegseth of high crimes and misdemeanours and abuse of power, alleging that he violated the War Powers Resolution by carrying out military operations against Iran and other countries without a declaration of war or specific authorisation from Congress.
## Background

The United States has been in a conflict with Iran since late February, with US forces carrying out strikes on Iranian targets as recently as last week. President Donald Trump has insisted the US is not at war, but has acknowledged that the conflict contributed to his party's heavy losses in the midterms, partly by pushing up petrol prices.
## What happens next
Impeachment would require a majority vote in the House, followed by a trial in the Senate.
more: Massie accuses Hegseth of an unauthorised war.
He introduced the articles on Monday.
Trump denies the US is at war with Iran.

stories.h: Diamond Platnumz and Zuchu welcome Davido and Chioma to Tanzania
stories.p: A video of Tanzanian star Diamond Platnumz and his wife Zuchu welcoming Davido and Chioma to Tanzania has gone viral, with fans praising Davido for carrying Chioma's bag.
body: Davido and his wife Chioma have arrived in Tanzania, where they were welcomed by Tanzanian music star Diamond Platnumz and his wife, singer Zuchu.
## The video

Footage shared on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, shows the two couples exchanging warm greetings after the Nigerians' arrival. One moment quickly became the talking point: Davido carrying Chioma's handbag and waiting while she got into her car, a gesture many fans said showed the strength of their relationship. The reason for the trip has not been officially announced.
## Background

Davido and Diamond Platnumz are two of Africa's biggest music stars and have collaborated before. Davido and Chioma held their widely celebrated wedding in Lagos in June 2024. The trip comes during an ongoing public feud between Davido and social media activist VeryDarkMan, who has been releasing videos and recordings aimed at the singer and his associates.
more: Diamond Platnumz and Zuchu welcomed the couple.
Davido was seen carrying Chioma's bag.
The trip comes amid his feud with VDM.

stories.h: Miss Universe Nigeria Danielle Adewusi arrives in Puerto Rico for 75th pageant
stories.p: Danielle Adewusi, crowned Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 in September, has arrived in Puerto Rico ahead of the 75th Miss Universe pageant on 24 November, where up to 120 countries will compete.
body: Nigeria's representative at Miss Universe 2026, Danielle Adewusi, has arrived in Puerto Rico ahead of the competition.
## The arrival

Her arrival was confirmed on the Miss Universe Nigeria Facebook page on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Adewusi was crowned Miss Universe Nigeria on 27 September at the Federal Palace Hotel in Victoria Island, Lagos, beating 19 other contestants while representing Lagos State.
## The pageant

The 75th Miss Universe pageant will hold on 24 November at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot in San Juan. The organisers say up to 120 countries and territories will take part, one of the largest fields in the competition's history.
## How to support her
Nigerians can support Adewusi through the fan vote and 'Beyond the Crown' categories, which are currently open.
## Background

Nigeria has never won Miss Universe. The country's best recent result came in 2024, when Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up, the highest placing by a Nigerian in the competition's history.
more: The pageant is on 24 November in San Juan.
Up to 120 countries will compete.
Fan voting is open.

stories.h: Lateef Adedimeji's praise for Tinubu's skills programmes divides fans
stories.p: Actor Lateef Adedimeji has drawn mixed reactions after posting a video praising President Tinubu's 3 Million Technical Talent and Skills Up Artisans programmes, with some fans calling it political.
body: Nollywood actor and filmmaker Lateef Adedimeji has sparked debate after speaking favourably about two of President Bola Tinubu's skills programmes.
## What he said

In a video posted on Instagram on Monday, 9 November 2026, Adedimeji spoke about the 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme and the Skills Up Artisans (SUPA) initiative, describing them as meaningful steps towards transforming Nigeria's tech and creative sectors. He encouraged his followers to position themselves to benefit from them.
## The reaction

Many followers focused on the timing of the video, with the 2027 elections approaching, and saw it as politically motivated. Some long-time fans expressed disappointment, while others said they still admired him and that he was entitled to share information about government programmes.
## Background

Adedimeji is one of the most popular actors in the Yoruba film industry and is married to actress Mo Bimpe. Several entertainers have openly backed the President's re-election, including Saidi Balogun and Eniola Badmus, and have also faced backlash online.
more: Adedimeji praised the 3MTT and SUPA programmes.
Some fans saw the video as political.
Others defended his right to share it.

stories.h: "Nigerians, please stop attacking my mum": Son of second wife accused of mistreating Mrs Anulika in Ukehe speaks out
stories.p: The son of the second wife accused of mistreating Mrs Gertrude Anulika Ngwu at her husband's Ozo ceremony in Ukehe, Enugu State, has begged Nigerians to stop attacking his mother online, saying she does not deserve the hate.
body: The son of the second wife at the centre of the viral Ukehe controversy has spoken out, begging Nigerians to stop attacking his mother.
## "Is it not enough already?"
"Nigerians, please stop attacking my mum. Is it not enough already? That woman does not deserve all this hate," he said.
"Do you want her to die? If anything happens to my mum, you people won't like it. Please, this is enough."
## How it started

His mother has faced a wave of criticism online since a video from his father's Ozo title-taking ceremony went viral. In the video, the second wife's children reportedly refused to spray money on the first wife, Mrs Gertrude Anulika Ngwu, despite repeated appeals from the master of ceremonies.
Claims then spread online that Mrs Anulika had endured years of mockery over being childless and had moved back to her father's home. Those claims have not been independently verified.
Since then, well-wishers have visited Mrs Anulika with gifts and money, and the Enugu governor's wife sent a representative with cash and promises of a house and a business.
## The other side of the story
The son's plea is a reminder that there are always two sides to a family story, and that online anger can quickly turn into harassment.

Sympathy for Mrs Anulika is understandable. But insults and threats against another woman, whose side of the story has not been heard, help no one. Families caught up in viral moments are still real people.
## Over to you
Has the online reaction to the Ukehe video gone too far? Can Nigerians support Mrs Anulika without attacking the other family?
more: The second wife's son says his mother is being attacked online.
He asked Nigerians to stop the hate.
The claims against his mother have not been verified.

stories.h: APC manifesto promises 50,000 police recruits, 200,000 homes and 10,000MW of power
stories.p: The APC has released President Tinubu's 109-page 2027 manifesto, 'From Reform to Prosperity Agenda 2027–2031', pledging 50,000 new police officers, 28,000 military recruits, 6% annual growth, 200,000 affordable homes and power generation approaching 10,000 megawatts.
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) has released President Bola Tinubu's manifesto for the 2027 presidential election, setting out his plans for a second term.
## The document

The 109-page manifesto, titled 'From Reform to Prosperity Agenda 2027–2031', was due to be formally unveiled at the Shehu Musa Yar'Adua Centre in Abuja on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. It covers security, the economy, housing, health and education, and says a second term would focus on turning the economic foundations of the first term into concrete gains for Nigerians.
## Security

The manifesto pledges to train and deploy 50,000 new police officers and work towards one officer for every 400 citizens, recruit 28,000 more military personnel, and complete four new Army divisions in Makurdi, Ilorin, Jalingo and Benin City. It proposes that the civil defence corps take over static guard duties from the police, the rollout of body cameras and forensic facilities, wider electronic surveillance of borders, and the deployment of forest guards, agro-rangers and mining marshals.
## Economy, housing and power

It targets annual economic growth of 6 per cent by 2031, halving youth unemployment, and extending credit to half of economically active Nigerians. It promises 200,000 affordable homes under a mass housing scheme and aims to raise available power generation towards 10,000 megawatts.
## Health and education

The plan aims to raise the share of functional primary health centres from 53 to 90 per cent, extend health insurance to 40 per cent of Nigerians, cut out-of-pocket health spending from 71 per cent to below 50 per cent, recruit 20,000 more teachers, halve the number of out-of-school children and expand the student loan scheme.
## Background

Tinubu faces 17 other presidential candidates, including Atiku Abubakar of the ADC, Peter Obi of the NDC and Seyi Makinde of the APM, in the election on 16 January 2027. Makinde launched his 'Reset Agenda' last week. Opposition candidates have criticised the government's record on the economy and insecurity, while the President says his reforms saved the economy from collapse.
more: The manifesto pledges 50,000 new police officers.
It promises 200,000 affordable homes.
It targets 6% annual growth by 2031.

stories.h: Orji Kalu says he once sold arms to anyone willing to pay, until his parents stopped him
stories.p: Former Abia governor Orji Uzor Kalu has said in a television interview that he previously sold weapons to individuals and countries that could pay, and stopped only after his parents told him to.
body: Former Abia State governor and senator Orji Uzor Kalu has said he once sold weapons to individuals and countries.
## What he said

Speaking in a television interview reported on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, Kalu said he sold arms to anyone willing to pay, and that he was interested only in making money at the time, not in how the weapons would be used. He said he stopped after his mother and father told him to. Asked whether he had supplied the African National Congress during the struggle against apartheid in South Africa, he said the ANC was not a specific customer and that he sold to anybody who wanted to buy. He did not say when the business took place or name any buyers.
## Background

Kalu, a businessman and politician, governed Abia State from 1999 to 2007 and later served as senator for Abia North. He was convicted of fraud in 2019, but the Supreme Court later set the conviction aside on technical grounds. He has recently been in the news over comments on the Senate presidency and predictions about the 2027 election.
more: Kalu says he sold arms to anyone who could pay.
He says he stopped at his parents' request.
He did not name buyers or dates.

stories.h: FRSC says 19,236 Nigerians died in road crashes since 2023
stories.p: The FRSC says 19,236 people died and 118,720 were injured in 37,789 road crashes across Nigeria between January 2023 and September 2026, with speeding and reckless driving the biggest killers.
body: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) says 19,236 Nigerians were killed in road crashes between January 2023 and September 2026.
## The figures

The FRSC's Abia State Sector Commander, Ngozi Ezeoma, told journalists on Monday, 9 November 2026, that there were 37,789 road crashes in the period, in which 118,720 people were injured. She said the figures came from the FRSC's Road Traffic Database Management System, and that speeding and human recklessness remain the biggest killers on Nigerian roads.
## Remembrance day

She spoke ahead of the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, which the United Nations marks on the third Sunday of November. She said the command would visit crash victims in selected hospitals as part of the commemoration.
## Background
Last week, actor Kunle Afod complained about the slow emergency response to a crash on the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway, although the Ogun State Government disputed his account.
more: 19,236 people died in 37,789 crashes.
118,720 people were injured.
Speeding is the biggest killer, the FRSC says.

stories.h: Manchester United expected to sack Michael Carrick with club in relegation zone
stories.p: Manchester United bosses are reportedly expected to recommend sacking head coach Michael Carrick, with the club in the Premier League relegation zone after 10 games. No final decision has been made.
body: Manchester United are increasingly expected to sack head coach Michael Carrick after a poor start to the 2026/27 season.
## What is reported

According to reports on Tuesday, 10 November 2026, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to recommend to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family that the 45-year-old be dismissed. No final decision has been made.
## Poor results

United had decided against sacking Carrick after a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October, giving him until the November international break to improve results. But the team is in the relegation zone after 10 Premier League matches. They drew 4-4 with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, after losing 2-0 to Chelsea and beating Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.
## Background
Carrick is a former United midfielder. The club has a huge following in Nigeria, where Premier League football is followed closely.
more: United are in the relegation zone after 10 games.
Bosses are expected to recommend Carrick's sacking.
No final decision has been made.

stories.h: Actress Toukie Smith, mother of Robert De Niro's twins, dies at 74
stories.p: Toukie Smith, known for the TV sitcom '227' and 'Miami Vice', has died in New York at 74 after a long battle with multiple sclerosis, her twins Airyn and Julian said.
body: American actress and model Toukie Smith has died at the age of 74.
## What happened

Her twins, Airyn and Julian, whom she shared with her former partner, actor Robert De Niro, said she died in New York on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, after a long and courageous battle with multiple sclerosis. The news was reported on Tuesday, 10 November.
## Her career

Smith was best known for playing Eva Rawley on the NBC sitcom '227', which she joined in 1989, first as a guest star. She also appeared in 'Miami Vice' and worked as a model, including in campaigns for Yves Saint Laurent. Born Dorris Smith in 1952, she took her stage name from a nickname given to her by her grandmother.
## Background
Smith and De Niro began dating in 1988, and their twins were born via a surrogate. The couple's on-off relationship ended in 1996.
more: Toukie Smith died at 74 in New York.
She had multiple sclerosis.
She starred in the sitcom '227'.

stories.h: Christmas return air tickets climb as high as ₦822,000 on some routes
stories.p: Return tickets on some domestic routes for the Christmas and New Year period have reached ₦822,000, with Air Peace listing about ₦676,000 for Lagos–Anambra return between 24 December and 2 January.
body: Nigerians planning to fly home for Christmas and the New Year are facing steep fares, with return tickets on some domestic routes reaching ₦822,000.
## The fares

According to checks reported on Monday, 9 November 2026, major carriers including Air Peace, United Nigeria Airlines and ValueJet have listed much higher fares for December 2026 and early January 2027, especially on routes linking Lagos and Abuja to the South-East and South-South. Air Peace listed a Lagos–Anambra return ticket between 24 December and 2 January at about ₦676,000, with the outbound flight at ₦341,500 and the return at ₦335,500. An Abuja–Anambra return costs about ₦677,000, and Lagos–Owerri about ₦671,000. The highest return fares found reached ₦822,000.
## Why fares rise

Demand for flights to the South-East and South-South surges every December as many Nigerians travel home for the holidays, weddings and other ceremonies. Airlines say the high cost of aviation fuel, foreign exchange for maintenance and leasing, and a shortage of aircraft push up prices.
## Background

Last week, one-way economy fares for flights around 20 and 21 December were reported at up to ₦337,500, increases of as much as 208 per cent. The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission previously accused some airlines of price-fixing during the 2025 festive season, which the airlines denied. Many travellers turn to road transport instead, despite security concerns on some highways.
## What it means
Travellers are being advised to book early to avoid the highest prices.
more: Some return fares have reached ₦822,000.
Lagos–Anambra return costs about ₦676,000 on Air Peace.
Demand peaks in late December.

stories.h: Court orders INEC chairman to produce Tinubu's 1999 and 2023 nomination forms in Sowore trial
stories.p: A Federal High Court in Abuja has subpoenaed INEC chairman Joash Amupitan to produce President Tinubu's nomination forms from 1999 and 2023 in the criminal trial of activist Omoyele Sowore, who is charged over social media posts about the President.
body: A Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash Amupitan, to produce President Bola Tinubu's nomination documents in the trial of activist Omoyele Sowore.
## The order

The subpoena, signed by Justice Mohammed Umar, directs the INEC chairman to present Tinubu's Form CF001 from his 1999 Lagos governorship campaign, which includes an affidavit relating to lost certificates, as well as the equivalent form submitted before the 2023 presidential election. It followed a ruling on Monday, 9 November 2026, approving a defence request to call Amupitan and Joe Igbokwe, a former publicity secretary of the APC in Lagos, as witnesses.
## The case

Sowore, the publisher of Sahara Reporters and a former presidential candidate, is being tried over social media posts in which he described the President as a criminal. His lawyers say they intend to call both men to testify. The trial is due to resume on 11 November.
## Background

Questions about Tinubu's academic records and early life have been raised by critics for years, and were the subject of legal challenges after the 2023 election, which the Supreme Court dismissed. The President and his supporters have consistently rejected claims of wrongdoing. Sowore has also faced other legal cases, including a separate cyberbullying trial in which a court recently rejected his bid to subpoena a DSS lawyer.
more: The court subpoenaed the INEC chairman.
He must produce Tinubu's 1999 and 2023 forms.
Sowore's trial resumes on 11 November.

stories.h: Jigawa declares holiday as Tinubu visits for rally and project launches
stories.p: Jigawa State declared Tuesday a public holiday for President Tinubu's first official visit since 2023. He is due to hold an APC rally and commission projects including an agricultural mechanisation programme with 400 tractors.
body: Jigawa State has declared Tuesday, 10 November 2026, a public holiday for a visit by President Bola Tinubu.
## The visit

Governor Umar Namadi told journalists in Dutse on Monday that the President would hold an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally and inaugurate four projects. He said it would be Tinubu's first official visit to the state since he took office in May 2023. The projects include a technical services centre, a skills acquisition centre named after the President, an agricultural mechanisation programme and a dualised road in Dutse.
## The farm equipment
The agricultural package includes 400 tractors, 60 combine harvesters, 150 boom sprayers and 150 seeders, along with other equipment intended to boost farm output in the state.
## Background

The Jigawa visit continues the President's campaign tour, which in the past week has taken him to Akwa Ibom, Rivers and Ebonyi states. Namadi, elected on the APC platform in 2023, is a strong supporter of the President's re-election. The North-West, which includes Jigawa, has one of the largest voting populations in Nigeria.
more: Tuesday is a public holiday in Jigawa.
Tinubu will commission four projects.
The package includes 400 tractors.

stories.h: White House briefly locked down after car crashes into barrier near Lafayette Park
stories.p: The White House was briefly locked down after a driver crashed a car into a security barrier at Lafayette Park and clashed with Secret Service agents and National Guard troops. Two people were arrested; President Trump was inside.
body: The White House was briefly placed on lockdown on Monday, 9 November 2026, after a car crashed into a security barrier near the complex.
## What happened

Shortly before 10am, a silver sedan mounted the pavement and hit a sign at the northern end of Lafayette Park, directly opposite the White House, according to reports. Witnesses said the driver got out and became involved in a physical confrontation with Secret Service agents and National Guard troops. Two people were arrested. The press area was locked down, reporters were ordered indoors, and roads around the park were closed. President Donald Trump was in the White House at the time. Officials said the driver was combative but was quickly arrested.
## Background

The incident came days after the Secret Service arrested an armed man near the White House who allegedly said voices had told him to kill the President. Officials have said the White House has seen a rise in security incidents, many linked to mental health problems. No motive for Monday's crash was given, and there were no reports of serious injuries.
more: A car crashed into a barrier near Lafayette Park.
Two people were arrested.
Trump was inside the White House.

stories.h: Tinubu mourns former ACN deputy national secretary Eteyen Amba
stories.p: President Tinubu has paid tribute to Chief Unanawao Eteyen Amba, a former deputy national secretary of the defunct Action Congress of Nigeria, describing him as a committed progressive who helped build the party.
body: President Bola Tinubu has mourned the death of Chief Unanawao Eteyen Amba, popularly known as Utrikang Oro, a former deputy national secretary of the defunct Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN).
## The tribute

In a condolence statement on Monday, 9 November 2026, the President described Amba as a committed progressive whose contributions to party building and Nigeria's democracy would not be forgotten. He recalled Amba's loyalty during the ACN's formative years and credited him with helping to shape the party's structures and political ideas, as well as offering wise counsel.
## Background

Tinubu was a leading figure in the ACN, which was one of the main opposition parties before it merged with other groups in 2013 to form the All Progressives Congress (APC). Details of the circumstances of Amba's death were not given in the statement.
more: Amba was ACN deputy national secretary.
Tinubu called him a committed progressive.
The ACN merged into the APC in 2013.

stories.h: 2027 Senate presidency: Orji Uzor Kalu says he cannot reject Tinubu's choice as political battle begins
stories.p: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu says he would accept the Senate presidency if President Tinubu backed him, adding his name to talk of the post going to the South-East after 2027, where Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma has also been linked to it.
body: Senator Orji Uzor Kalu has openly said he would be willing to become Nigeria's next Senate President, and would have no reason to turn down the position if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu backed him for it.
## "I can't say no"

The former Abia State governor, who represents Abia North Senatorial District, made the statement in a television interview, as talk about the leadership of the next National Assembly begins to gather pace ahead of the 2027 general elections.
"If Tinubu chooses me as the next Senate President, I can't say no," Kalu said.
Brief as it was, the statement has added another twist to the political calculations already taking shape within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
## Zoning to the South-East?

For some time, there has been talk of zoning the next Senate presidency to the South-East. Nothing has been officially agreed, but that has not stopped political figures from being linked to the position.

One of the names being mentioned is Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, who served as senator for Imo West before becoming governor. His reported interest has sparked political conversation, given his influence within the APC and his relationship with the party's national leadership.
There have also been reports of reactions involving FCT Minister Nyesom Wike, although the extent of any disagreement over the position remains unclear.
## Kalu versus Uzodimma
Both Kalu and Uzodimma are experienced politicians from the South-East. Both have served in the Senate, and both have strong relationships within the ruling party.

The big question is whether the APC will actually zone the Senate presidency to the South-East in 2027, and if so, who will win the party's backing. For now, there is no official confirmation that the position has been reserved for the region.
## The senators decide
It is worth remembering that the President has no constitutional power to appoint the Senate President. Senators elect their presiding officer themselves when a new National Assembly is inaugurated.
Even so, presidential support and internal party negotiations often play a major role in deciding who eventually emerges.

Whether Kalu's remarks signal serious ambition or simply a willingness to serve if called upon remains to be seen. What is clear is that the race for the leadership of the next National Assembly is already attracting attention, even before Nigerians go to the polls.
## Over to you
If the Senate presidency is zoned to the South-East, who would be the better choice: Orji Uzor Kalu or Hope Uzodimma?
more: Kalu says he would accept the Senate presidency if Tinubu backed him.
Hope Uzodimma has also been linked to the position.
Senators, not the President, elect the Senate President.

stories.h: "My hair costs more than my clothes": Davido's elder sister, Sharon Adeleke, says she doesn't believe in spending big on outfits
stories.p: Davido's elder sister, Sharon Adeleke, says she would rather spend good money on her hair than on expensive designer clothes. She also revealed that her own wedding dress cost just $2,000, and that her outfit for Davido and Chioma's white wedding was a last-minute rescue.
body: Davido's elder sister, Sharon Adeleke, has opened up about her fashion choices, revealing that she would rather spend good money on her hair than buy expensive designer clothes.
## "My hair costs more than my clothes"
Speaking on a podcast, Sharon said she has never really believed in spending a fortune on clothing, no matter how much money a person has.
She enjoys looking good, especially when it comes to her hair, but she does not see the need to attach an expensive price tag to every outfit.
## The wedding outfit drama
Sharon also spoke about her appearance at Davido and Chioma's white wedding, revealing that things did not go as smoothly as she had planned.

She said she had hired a stylist and a fashion designer to handle her outfit, but they failed to deliver as expected. Everything ended up as a last-minute arrangement, leaving her with little choice but to hope it worked out. At some point, she said, it was simply a case of "God abeg!"
## A $2,000 wedding dress
She also shared an interesting detail about her own wedding. Despite coming from one of Nigeria's wealthiest and best-known families, she said her husband spent just $2,000 on her wedding dress.
She added that she personally paid for the dresses worn by all 13 of her bridesmaids.
## Not what people expect
Her revelations are interesting because many people assume wealthy families spend outrageous amounts on everything they wear.
Now imagine Davido's own elder sister saying she doesn't believe in buying expensive clothes, while some people borrow money just to wear designer labels and impress strangers.
## Over to you
Do you agree with Sharon that expensive clothes are unnecessary, even when you can comfortably afford them?
more: Sharon Adeleke says her hair costs more than her clothes.
Her own wedding dress reportedly cost $2,000.
She paid for all 13 of her bridesmaids' dresses.

stories.h: Woman confronts herder after cattle destroy her farm crops in Nasarawa State
stories.p: A woman in Nasarawa State has confronted a herder after his cattle strayed onto her farmland and destroyed crops she had spent months growing. The incident has reopened the question of who pays when a farmer's livelihood is wiped out.
body: A woman in Nasarawa State has confronted a herder after his cattle entered her farmland and destroyed crops she had spent months cultivating.
## Months of work gone
For someone who depends on farming to survive, watching cattle destroy months of hard work can be heartbreaking.

Imagine spending your money on seeds, preparing the land, planting and waiting patiently for harvest, only to wake up one day and find your crops destroyed. Worse still, many farmers borrow money to cultivate their land, hoping to repay the loan after harvest.
## An old source of tension
Incidents like this remain one of the main causes of tension between farmers and herders in parts of Nigeria, and some have escalated into violence in the past.
The question is: who compensates the woman for her losses? Who takes responsibility for the destroyed crops?
## Protection for everyone
Farmers deserve protection, just as herders have a right to carry out their lawful activities. But nobody should be allowed to destroy another person's livelihood without consequences.
Clear rules on grazing, quick ways to settle disputes and fair compensation could help prevent confrontations like this from turning into something worse.
## Over to you
If cattle destroy a farmer's crops, should the owner be made to pay full compensation?
more: The woman confronted a herder over destroyed crops.
The incident happened in Nasarawa State.
Who should pay for the farmer's losses?

stories.h: Destiny Etiko reportedly appointed Senior Special Assistant to Enugu Governor Peter Mbah
stories.p: Nollywood actress Destiny Etiko has reportedly been appointed by Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah as his Senior Special Assistant on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy, taking her beyond the film industry and into public service.
body: Popular Nollywood actress Destiny Etiko has reportedly secured a political appointment in Enugu State, with reports saying Governor Peter Mbah has named her Senior Special Assistant on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy.
If confirmed, the appointment would mark a new chapter in the actress's career, taking her beyond the movie industry and into public service.
## A familiar face

Destiny Etiko has built a strong reputation in Nollywood over the years, becoming one of the industry's most recognisable faces. With millions of followers across social media, she has also become an influential personality, particularly among young Nigerians.
## What the role involves
Her new role is expected to involve supporting youth engagement programmes, encouraging young talent and helping to develop Enugu State's growing creative economy.

There is plenty of work to be done. Enugu has a rich history in entertainment, arts and culture. With the right support, the state could create more opportunities for young filmmakers, musicians, content creators and others trying to earn a living from their creativity.
## Celebrity appointment or real impact?
The real question is how much influence and responsibility the actress will have in shaping those opportunities.
Celebrity appointments often attract public attention, but what matters in the long run is the impact they make on ordinary people.
For Destiny Etiko, this could be a chance to use her popularity, industry experience and connections to help young people who are struggling to find their feet in entertainment.
## Over to you
What do you think of Governor Peter Mbah's decision to bring Destiny Etiko into his administration? Is this a good move for Enugu's creative industry?
more: Destiny Etiko was reportedly named SSA on Youth Engagement and Creative Economy.
The appointment is by Enugu Governor Peter Mbah.
Her role will focus on young creatives in Enugu.

stories.h: INEC removes over 1.6 million invalid registrants from voter register
stories.p: INEC says it has removed 1,608,660 invalid registrants and 876 dead voters from the register after a public review of the preliminary list. The cleaned-up register will be published on 16 December.
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608,660 invalid registrants from Nigeria's voter register.
## What INEC announced

The commission said on Monday, 9 November 2026, that the removals followed complaints, objections and claims submitted by the public after it displayed the preliminary voter register in October. It also deleted the records of 876 voters confirmed to have died, after verifying claims submitted during the review. INEC said the display of the preliminary register was meant to allow citizens and civil society groups to flag errors, duplicates and other irregularities.
## What happens next
INEC said it will publish the final, cleaned-up register on 16 December 2026, as required by the Electoral Act. The commission expects more than 103 million registered voters for the 2027 elections.
## Background

The figure is in line with the roughly 1.5 million questionable records INEC said earlier it had identified. A former INEC director, Oluwole Osaze-Uzzi, questioned last week how so many invalid entries could have entered the register despite biometric safeguards, and called on the commission to explain how they were detected. Opposition parties have also raised concerns about alleged AI-generated photographs in the register.
## Why it matters
A credible voter register is key to public confidence in the 16 January 2027 presidential election.
more: 1,608,660 invalid registrants were removed.
876 dead voters were also deleted.
The final register will be published on 16 December.

stories.h: Chief Justice swears in 375 judges for 2027 election tribunals
stories.p: Chief Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun has sworn in 375 judges to serve on election petition tribunals for 2027, warning them to resist political pressure and cautioning politicians and lawyers against abusing ex parte applications.
body: The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has sworn in 375 judges who will serve on the election petition tribunals for the 2027 general elections.
## The ceremony

The swearing-in took place on Monday, 9 November 2026, at the Body of Benchers auditorium in Abuja, alongside the launch of the second edition of the Judicial Electoral Manual and a training workshop for judicial officers.
## The CJN's warning

Justice Kekere-Ekun charged the judges to uphold judicial independence, resist political pressure and deliver justice without fear or favour, in line with the Constitution, judicial ethics and the rule of law. She also warned political parties, lawyers, the media and the public against behaviour aimed at undermining the judicial process, and specifically cautioned against the abuse of ex parte applications, which are orders granted without hearing the other side.
## Background

Election petition tribunals hear challenges to the results of governorship, National Assembly and state assembly elections. Courts have played a major role in recent Nigerian elections, and pre-election cases are already shaping the 2027 contest, including a Federal High Court ruling that voided Atiku Abubakar's ADC nomination, which the party has appealed, and a ruling on the Imo West Senate ticket. Concerns about conflicting court orders, especially ex parte orders, have been raised repeatedly in recent years.
more: 375 judges were sworn in for election tribunals.
The CJN warned against abuse of ex parte orders.
A new Judicial Electoral Manual was launched.

stories.h: Victor Umeh: Any Igbo person against Peter Obi is an enemy of the Igbo
stories.p: Senator Victor Umeh of the NDC has said any Igbo person who campaigns against Peter Obi's presidential bid is an enemy of the Igbo people, and urged the South-East to unite behind him. He also cautioned the Anambra government.
body: Senator Victor Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, has warned that any Igbo person working against Peter Obi's presidential ambition is an enemy of the Igbo people.
## What he said

In a video that circulated on Monday, 9 November 2026, Umeh, a member of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), described Obi as the conscience of the Igbo people in the 2027 election and urged South-East residents to unite behind his bid. He cautioned political leaders in the region, particularly the Anambra State Government, against actions that could undermine Obi's campaign.
## Background

Obi, a former Anambra governor, is the NDC's presidential candidate, with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. While he remains popular in the South-East, several of the region's governors have declared support for President Bola Tinubu. Anambra Governor Charles Soludo's APGA last week adopted Tinubu as its candidate and promised him half of the state's votes, while Ebonyi Governor Francis Nwifuru on Monday promised Tinubu 80 per cent of Ebonyi's votes. The NDC in Anambra has set a target of 98 per cent of the state's votes for Obi.
## Reactions
The Anambra government had not publicly responded at the time of writing.
## Yul Edochie responds

Actor Yul Edochie, a supporter of President Tinubu, challenged Umeh in a video on 10 November, saying he respected the senator but that such remarks could make Igbo people see one another as enemies. He said political choice is a personal right, and noted that Tinubu and Seyi Makinde are both from the South-West, yet no Yoruba leader has called supporters of either man enemies of the region.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Umeh says Obi is the conscience of the Igbo.
He cautioned the Anambra government.
Several South-East governors back Tinubu.

stories.h: Viral image of Peter Obi in hospital after gym injury is AI-generated, checks show
stories.p: A viral image claiming NDC candidate Peter Obi was admitted to hospital after a treadmill injury has been found to be AI-generated, according to a fact-check using several detection tools. Obi's camp had earlier denied the report.
body: A viral image claiming that Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), was in hospital after a gym injury has been found to be fake.
## The claim

The image was posted on X on Sunday, 1 November 2026, with a caption claiming Obi had injured his neck on a treadmill and been admitted to hospital. By Monday, 9 November, the post had been viewed more than 67,000 times, and similar posts had spread on other platforms.
## The fact-check

According to a fact-check published on Monday, a reverse image search linked the picture to similar claims on other platforms, suggesting a wider effort to spread it. Several AI-detection tools found a high probability that the image was AI-generated, and a further check indicated it had been created with an AI image tool.
## Background

Obi's campaign had earlier denied reports that he broke his neck in a gym accident, and the former Anambra governor has continued to campaign publicly, including at airports and rallies in recent days. Opposition parties have raised concerns about alleged AI-generated images in the voter register.
## Why it matters
Fake images and videos of candidates are expected to be a growing problem in the 2027 campaign.
more: The image claimed Obi was hospitalised after a gym injury.
Detection tools found it was AI-generated.
Obi's camp had earlier denied the report.

stories.h: INEC warns against 'Rig and Die' slogan ahead of 2027 elections, raises concerns over electoral violence
stories.p: INEC has raised serious concern over the growing use of the "Rig and Die" slogan by some political actors ahead of the 2027 elections, warning that such language could encourage violence. But the slogan also points to a deeper problem: Nigerians' fear that their votes will not count.
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has expressed serious concern over the growing use of the controversial "Rig and Die" slogan by some political actors ahead of Nigeria's 2027 general elections.
## A dangerous slogan
According to the electoral body, such language is dangerous and could encourage political violence, putting innocent Nigerians at risk as the country prepares for another major election.
## Why it has come to this
The controversy also raises a question that cannot be ignored: why has Nigeria's electoral system reached a point where political actors feel the need to use such threatening language?

For years, Nigerians have complained about electoral malpractice, vote buying, intimidation, ballot box snatching and alleged manipulation of results. Many voters have grown frustrated, especially when they believe their votes do not count.
With the 2027 elections approaching, political tensions are already building.
## Confidence in the process
INEC is right to warn against inflammatory statements that could endanger lives. But the commission must also recognise that public confidence in the electoral process remains a major concern.
Nigerians want elections where votes are counted honestly, results are transmitted transparently, and those caught manipulating the process face real consequences.
Political leaders, too, have a responsibility to avoid statements that could turn ordinary citizens into victims of electoral violence.
No election should cost an innocent Nigerian their life. At the same time, electoral offenders must never be allowed to operate without consequences.
## Over to you
Should INEC be more concerned about the slogan "Rig and Die", or about fixing the electoral weaknesses that make Nigerians fear rigging in the first place?
more: INEC warns the 'Rig and Die' slogan could fuel violence.
Many Nigerians fear their votes will not count.
Electoral offenders must face real consequences.

stories.h: Beautiful moment as former Aviation Minister Osita Chidoka celebrates his father's 100th birthday with family
stories.p: Former Aviation Minister Osita Chidoka's father has reached the remarkable age of 100, with family members coming together to celebrate his birthday and the gift of long life.
body: Reaching 100 years of age is no small blessing, and for the family of former Aviation Minister Osita Chidoka, it is a moment truly worth celebrating.
## A century of life
The former minister's father has reached the remarkable age of 100, and family members have come together to celebrate his birthday and the gift of long life.

Photos from the celebration show the centenarian seated on an ornate chair in flowing white traditional attire, with coral beads around his neck, a red cap resting on his lap and a walking stick in hand.

Just imagine living for an entire century. The things he must have witnessed, the changes Nigeria has gone through, the generations he has watched grow, and the countless memories gathered along the way.
## A special blessing
For his children, grandchildren and other loved ones, having their father around at 100 is something truly special. Many families would give anything for such an opportunity.
Happy 100th birthday to Papa Chidoka! May his remaining years be filled with peace, good health and happiness.
## Over to you
Are you fortunate enough to have a parent or grandparent who has reached 90 or even 100 years? Share your story.
more: Osita Chidoka's father has turned 100.
The family gathered to celebrate the milestone.
Chidoka is a former Minister of Aviation.

stories.h: All is fair in war, but has VeryDarkMan gone too far with Davido?
stories.p: Amid his ongoing disagreement with Davido, VeryDarkMan has reportedly brought up the deaths of the singer's late friends, a painful chapter long surrounded by unproven rumours. Criticism is fair, but should personal tragedy ever be used as ammunition?
body: VeryDarkMan (VDM) does not seem to believe in fighting fairly. When he has a disagreement with someone, he appears willing to go to any length to make his point, even if it means bringing up some of the most painful moments in that person's life.
## A painful chapter
Over the years, Davido has lost several close friends and associates in tragic circumstances. Their deaths set off all kinds of rumours and conspiracy theories online.

Some people even claimed the deaths were connected to rituals or sacrifices for fame and success. None of those claims was ever proven, and there is no credible evidence linking Davido to any of their deaths.

Imagine losing people who were very close to you, only to have strangers turn their deaths into accusations against you. Davido has lived with those memories for years. He has carried on with his music career, built his family and moved forward with his life, but moving forward does not mean the pain has disappeared.
## Reopening old wounds
Now, amid his ongoing disagreement with Davido, VDM has reportedly brought those painful memories back into public discussion. This is where things appear to be getting out of hand.

You can criticise Davido's music, lifestyle, public statements or behaviour. You can disagree with him and challenge his opinions. That is perfectly normal. But bringing up the deaths of his close friends because of a disagreement raises serious questions.
What exactly is the intention? Is it to expose wrongdoing, to make a legitimate point, or simply to hurt someone where he is most vulnerable?
## Where are the limits?

VDM has built a reputation for confronting people without holding back, and his supporters may argue he is only giving his opponents the same treatment they give others. But surely there should be limits.

Davido is not above criticism, and neither is VeryDarkMan. Both are public figures who should be held accountable for their actions. Using someone's personal tragedies as ammunition in a public quarrel, however, is something else entirely.

There are some experiences people never fully recover from. They may laugh and smile in public, but that does not mean they have forgotten. If winning an argument requires reopening another person's deepest wounds, perhaps the argument has already gone too far.
## Over to you

People say all is fair in love and war, but does that mean we should abandon all compassion when we disagree with someone? Has VDM crossed the line with Davido, or is this just two public figures fighting without limits?
more: VDM has reportedly raised the deaths of Davido's late friends.
Rumours about those deaths were never proven.
Is personal tragedy fair game in a public feud?

stories.h: Wike promises ₦10m to each councillor whose ward delivers votes for Tinubu
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly promised ₦10 million to every councillor across Nigeria whose ward votes for President Tinubu in the 2027 election, speaking at an event in Kwali Area Council.
body: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has reportedly promised a ₦10 million reward to each councillor in Nigeria whose ward votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.
## What he said

Wike made the pledge during a political engagement in Kwali Area Council of the Federal Capital Territory, according to reports on Monday, 9 November 2026. He also praised his Rainbow Coalition, saying it was bringing together politicians from across the country, and urged residents of Kwali and the wider FCT to back the President's re-election, arguing that a second term would bring more development to Abuja.
## Background

Wike, a former Rivers governor and PDP chieftain, leads the Rainbow Coalition of politicians from the PDP and other parties backing Tinubu. He has been one of the President's most vocal campaigners, frequently criticising opposition candidates Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar.
## Why it matters
INEC this week also warned political actors against inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the elections.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Wike pledged ₦10m per councillor whose ward backs Tinubu.
He spoke in Kwali Area Council, FCT.
He praised his Rainbow Coalition.

stories.h: Tunde Bakare says he turned down Tinubu's offer of a ministerial post
stories.p: Pastor Tunde Bakare says President Tinubu offered him a cabinet position, which he declined because he felt too old for the job, preferring to advise the government from the background. He says he is not part of the opposition.
body: Pastor Tunde Bakare, leader of the Citadel Global Community Church, says President Bola Tinubu offered him a ministerial position, which he turned down.
## What he said

Speaking at an event in Leicester, United Kingdom, on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Bakare said he told the President he was too old for the demands of the office and would rather work quietly in the background. He said he offered instead to give advice and raise concerns wherever he believed government policy had fallen short. He insisted that not being in the cabinet did not make him part of the opposition, describing his approach as a 'propositional platform' focused on identifying problems and proposing solutions.
## Background

Bakare was Muhammadu Buhari's running mate in the 2011 presidential election and sought the APC presidential ticket in 2022, which Tinubu won. He has been an outspoken commentator on national affairs for decades and has had a mixed relationship with successive governments.
more: Bakare says Tinubu offered him a cabinet post.
He declined, saying he was too old.
He says he is not in the opposition.

stories.h: Russell Brand jailed for 10 and a half years for rape and sexual assaults
stories.p: British comedian Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after a jury found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He had denied the charges.
body: British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison.
## The sentence

Brand, 51, was sentenced on Monday, 9 November 2026, after a jury of eight men and four women found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others, in offences dating back to 2004. He was cleared of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. Brand had maintained his innocence, saying all his encounters were consensual.
## The judge's remarks

Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand had shown a casual and arrogant disregard for women's right to say no, and placed the crimes in the context of his rise to fame about 20 years ago, when he was widely seen as clever, funny and charismatic.
## Background

Brand became famous in the 2000s as a stand-up comedian, television and radio presenter and Hollywood actor, and was known for his outrageous on-air behaviour and his public battles with drug and alcohol addiction. The allegations against him first emerged in a joint media investigation in 2023, after which he was charged by British police. In recent years he had reinvented himself as an online commentator with a large following.
more: Brand was jailed for 10 years and six months.
He was convicted of rape and three sexual assaults.
He was cleared of three other counts.

stories.h: Seven dead and over 100 injured in Egypt train collision near Cairo
stories.p: At least seven people were killed and about 125 injured when a passenger train crashed into the rear of another in Giza province, south of Cairo. Prosecutors have opened an investigation.
body: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured in a collision between two passenger trains in Egypt.
## What happened

The crash happened on Sunday, 8 November 2026, in the al-Ayyat district of Giza province, about 52 kilometres south of Cairo. According to Egypt's Transportation Ministry, a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the back of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, derailing several carriages and trapping passengers. The Health Ministry said 125 people were injured. Emergency services sent 72 ambulances, and local residents helped pull survivors from the wreckage.
## Investigation
Egypt's Public Prosecution has opened an investigation into the cause of the crash.
## Background
Egypt has one of Africa's oldest and busiest railway networks, but it has a long history of deadly accidents, often blamed on poor maintenance and human error.
more: Seven people were killed and about 125 injured.
One train crashed into the back of another.
Prosecutors are investigating.

stories.h: Funke Akindele says influencer rejected her paid offer to promote 'Everybody Loves Jenifa'
stories.p: Filmmaker Funke Akindele says an unnamed influencer turned down her paid offer to promote 'Everybody Loves Jenifa', and ignored her follow-up messages, while speaking at a creative industry panel.
body: Nollywood filmmaker Funke Akindele has revealed that a social media influencer turned down her paid offer to promote her blockbuster film 'Everybody Loves Jenifa'.
## What she said

Speaking at a panel session at the Creative Africa Nexus Weekend, in a video shared online on 7 November 2026, Akindele said she had been reluctant to approach influencers but eventually decided to try. She proposed that the influencer post about the film several times a week during the promotional campaign, and offered to pay. However, the influencer's management turned her down, and when she followed up to make clear she was willing to pay, her message was ignored. She did not name the influencer.
## Background

'Everybody Loves Jenifa' was one of the biggest Nollywood box-office hits. Akindele, one of the industry's most successful filmmakers, is now promoting her new film 'The Four', which recently sold out its London premiere. Influencer marketing has become a major part of how Nigerian films are promoted, with content creators often paid to make videos about new releases.
more: Funke offered to pay the influencer.

stories.h: Odumodublvck says he refused to settle with man suing him over alleged assault
stories.p: Rapper Odumodublvck says a man who repeatedly filmed him without permission has taken him to court, accusing him of assault, and that he rejected his lawyers' advice to settle out of court.
body: Rapper Odumodublvck has spoken about a court case brought against him by a man he says repeatedly filmed him without permission.
## His account

According to reports on Monday, 9 November 2026, the rapper said the man gained access to his home through a mutual friend and began filming him without his consent, continuing even after warnings from him and his bouncer. He said the disagreement continued at a party when the man brought out his camera again, and that he confronted him on stage, but that they later settled their differences, with the man even dancing with him while still filming. Odumodublvck said he was surprised when the man later took him to court, accusing him of assault.
## Refusing to settle
The rapper said his lawyers advised him to settle the matter out of court, but he refused. The man's side of the story has not been reported, and the allegations have not been tested in court.
## Background
Odumodublvck, is an Abuja-based rapper known for hits such as 'Declan Rice'. He went viral last week after a brief encounter with Peter Obi at Abuja airport.

stories.h: Obi says NFF officials stopped him from greeting world champion Flamingos
stories.p: NDC candidate Peter Obi says Nigeria Football Federation officials refused to let him congratulate the Flamingos when he saw them at Abuja airport on their return with the U-17 World Cup trophy. The NFF had not responded.
body: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has accused officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) of stopping him from congratulating the Flamingos after their World Cup triumph.
## What Obi said

Obi said he was at the airport in Abuja at about 7am on Monday, 9 November 2026, to catch a flight to Enugu, when he saw the Flamingos, who had just arrived with the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup trophy. He said he asked his protocol officer to find out if he could go over and welcome the players, but was told that NFF officials had refused, reportedly warning that anyone who allowed him near the team would lose their job.
## 'Not the first time'

Obi said this was not the first time he had been prevented from supporting a national team. He recalled travelling to Uyo in March 2025 to watch a World Cup qualifier against Zimbabwe, and said that although he was warmly received before the match, he was not allowed the same access afterwards.
## Background

The Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in the final in Rabat on Saturday to become the first African team to win the tournament, and were welcomed back to Nigeria on Monday. President Bola Tinubu and the First Lady have both congratulated the team.
## Presidency responds

The Presidency accused Obi of trying to politicise national sports teams. In a post on X on Monday, the President's special assistant on social media, Dada Olusegun, said the national teams, including the Under-17 girls, represent the whole country and not any party or individual's ambitions, and that protocol rules around national teams are designed to protect young athletes from political exploitation, commercial distractions and media pressure. The NFF itself had not publicly commented.
more: Obi says he saw the Flamingos at Abuja airport.
He says NFF officials refused his request to greet them.
The NFF has not responded.

stories.h: Nwifuru promises Tinubu 80% of Ebonyi votes at Abakaliki rally
stories.p: Ebonyi governor Francis Nwifuru told President Tinubu at an APC rally in Abakaliki that Ebonyi is an APC state and that 80% of its votes are assured for him in 2027.
body: Ebonyi State governor Francis Nwifuru has promised President Bola Tinubu 80 per cent of the state's votes in the 2027 presidential election.
## What he said

Speaking at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential rally in Abakaliki on Monday, 9 November 2026, Nwifuru told the President that Ebonyi was an APC state, that 80 per cent of its votes were assured for him and that he would win by a landslide.
## Background

The rally is part of Tinubu's campaign tour of the South-East and South-South, which has included stops in Akwa Ibom and Rivers states in the past week. Several South-East governors have declared support for the President, and the APGA in Anambra has also adopted him as its candidate. The South-East, however, is the home region of NDC candidate Peter Obi, who won most of the region's votes in 2023, and his party has set ambitious targets of its own, including 98 per cent of Anambra's votes.
## How people reacted
The governor's pledge drew mixed reactions on social media. Supporters of the President welcomed it, while others questioned whether any governor could guarantee how residents would vote.
## What happens next
The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: Nwifuru says 80% of Ebonyi votes are assured for Tinubu.
He spoke at an APC rally in Abakaliki.
Critics questioned whether votes can be guaranteed.

stories.h: Osun government offices shut as NLC begins three-day strike over council funds
stories.p: Government offices and public schools in Osogbo were shut on Monday as workers in Osun began a three-day strike in solidarity with local government employees over withheld statutory allocations to the state's councils.
body: Government offices in Osun State were shut on Monday, 9 November 2026, as workers began a three-day strike over withheld allocations to local governments.
## What happened

The gates of the state government secretariat and the House of Assembly in Osogbo were locked, with no workers or business activity at either, according to reports. Local government secretariats in Olorunda and Osogbo were also closed, and pupils in public schools in Osogbo were sent home after teachers joined the strike.
## Why workers are striking

In a statement on Sunday, the state chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), led by its chairman, Christopher Arapasopo, directed all affiliated unions to join the strike in solidarity with the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE). The NLC said the action followed the expiry of a seven-day ultimatum to the federal and Osun state governments over the continued withholding of statutory allocations to local councils in the state, which it said remained unresolved.
## Background

Osun's local governments have been at the centre of a long legal and political dispute over who controls the councils, which has led to federal allocations being withheld. Osun is governed by Ademola Adeleke, who has backed President Bola Tinubu's re-election.
more: The strike is due to last three days.
Workers want withheld council allocations released.
Schools in Osogbo sent pupils home.

stories.h: Naira up about 6% against the dollar in a year as reserves reach $55bn
stories.p: The naira has strengthened by about 6.3% against the US dollar over the past year, trading at about ₦1,347 on 6 November compared with ₦1,437 a year earlier, while Nigeria's foreign reserves have risen to about $55.1 billion.
body: The naira has gained ground against the US dollar over the past year, according to official exchange rate data.
## The figures

The naira traded at about ₦1,346.79 to the dollar on 6 November 2026, compared with ₦1,436.74 on the same date in 2025, a gain of about ₦90, or 6.26 per cent, according to reports on Monday, 9 November. Nigeria's external reserves have risen to about $55.13 billion.
## Why it matters

A stronger naira could reduce the cost of imported raw materials, machinery, medicines and other goods priced in foreign currency. However, how quickly that feeds through to lower prices for consumers depends on businesses passing on the savings.
## Background

The naira lost much of its value after the government unified the exchange rate in 2023, when the official rate was about ₦461 to the dollar. The Central Bank of Nigeria has since taken steps to stabilise the foreign exchange market and improve dollar supply. The naira's performance has become a campaign issue: President Bola Tinubu said last week that it would have become worthless without his reforms, while the campaign of APM candidate Seyi Makinde said the President could not claim credit for a recovery after policies that weakened it.
more: The naira gained about ₦90 against the dollar in a year.
Reserves are about $55.1 billion.
The naira's value has become a campaign issue.

stories.h: Hackers claim leaked Russian records show up to 450,000 war deaths in Ukraine
stories.p: Two hacking groups say records taken from Russia's state statistics agency show between about 394,000 and 450,000 Russian deaths linked to the war in Ukraine. The figures have not been verified and the agency denies any data was leaked.
body: Two hacking groups say they have obtained records from Russia's state statistics agency pointing to hundreds of thousands of Russian deaths in the war in Ukraine.
## The claims

According to reports on Monday, 9 November 2026, the pro-Ukrainian group Silent Crow and the Belarusian Cyber Partisans said they accessed an internal database at Rosstat containing information from death certificates from February 2022 to August 2026. Silent Crow, which published the data, put the death toll at about 450,100, while the Belarusian Cyber Partisans, using a narrower method that counted only records naming military operations as the cause of death, put it at 393,881. The figures have not been independently verified.
## Russia's response

Rosstat acknowledged that its systems were targeted between 29 October and 1 November but said no databases were compromised. Russia has banned both groups as 'extremist organisations'. Moscow has rarely given official figures for its military losses.
## Background

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Independent estimates of Russian military deaths have varied widely, and both sides have been accused of under-reporting their own losses. The Belarusian Cyber Partisans also oppose the government of Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, a close ally of Moscow.
more: The groups claim up to 450,000 Russian deaths.
The figures have not been verified.
Rosstat denies any data was leaked.

stories.h: Soldier, teenager and two others killed in fresh Plateau attack
stories.p: Gunmen reportedly killed a soldier and three residents, including a 15-year-old boy, in an attack on Bell village in Sho community, Barkin Ladi LGA of Plateau State, on Sunday night.
body: Gunmen have reportedly killed a soldier and three residents, including a 15-year-old boy, in an attack on a village in Plateau State.
## What happened

The attack took place at about 9pm on Sunday, 8 November 2026, in Bell village, Sho community, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area. A resident said the attackers stormed the village and opened fire on residents, leaving some dead and others injured. A local youth association confirmed the killings, identifying three of the victims, aged 15, 28 and 32.
## Official response
The police and the military had not publicly commented on the attack at the time of writing.
## Background

Barkin Ladi and other parts of Plateau State have suffered repeated deadly attacks on rural communities in recent years. On Sunday, APM presidential candidate Seyi Makinde visited Angwan Rukuba in Jos North to console families of 33 people killed in an attack in March. Bishop David Oyedepo also warned politicians last week about the failure to stop killings and kidnappings.
more: A soldier and three residents were reportedly killed.
One victim was 15 years old.
The attack happened in Barkin Ladi LGA.

stories.h: Gospel singer Toluwanisings buried in Ibadan after family dispute
stories.p: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, is being buried in Ibadan on Monday, almost four weeks after his death, following a dispute between his widow and his family that police helped resolve.
body: Gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, is being laid to rest in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Monday, 9 November 2026.
## The arrangements

According to funeral details shared on the singer's official Instagram page, the lying-in-state was scheduled for 9am to 10am, followed by a burial service from 10am to 11am at an event centre on Hope Road, Alakia, Ibadan. The announcement did not say where he would be interred.
## The dispute

Toluwanisings died in the early hours of 14 October 2026. His burial was delayed by weeks of disagreement between his widow and his family over the arrangements, reportedly including where he should be buried. The Oyo State Police Command stepped in after learning of the dispute on 28 October, with Commissioner of Police Olugbenga Abimbola helping the two sides reach an agreement.
## The burial

Videos from Monday's ceremony showed pallbearers in black suits carrying the singer's white casket, led by trumpeters, before he was taken to his home, where a private burial was held. Some fans remarked on the absence of fellow gospel artistes at the ceremony.
## Background
Toluwanisings was a Nigerian gospel singer. The public dispute over his burial attracted wide attention.
more: The burial is in Ibadan on 9 November.
He died on 14 October.
Police helped resolve a family dispute.

stories.h: "Pharaoh, let my people go!": Cubana Chief Priest replies Umahi, accuses him of giving Tinubu fake promises on South-East votes
stories.p: Cubana Chief Priest has fired back at Works Minister David Umahi, nicknaming him "Pharaoh" and accusing him of making empty promises to President Tinubu about South-East votes. He also claimed Umahi is preparing his son to become Ebonyi governor, and mocked him with his own "money na water" catchphrase.
body: Socialite and businessman Cubana Chief Priest has replied Minister of Works David Umahi, a day after the minister mocked his famous "money na water" catchphrase and asked how many people he has given scholarships.
## "Pharaoh, let my people go"
Borrowing from the Bible story of Moses and Pharaoh, Cubana Chief Priest gave the minister a new nickname, and accused him of making promises to President Bola Tinubu that he cannot deliver.
"Pharaoh, let my people go. Stop giving Tinubu fake promises on votes. What project are you using to convince South-East people to vote for him?" he said.
## The governorship claim
He went further, claiming that Umahi is preparing his son to become governor of Ebonyi State after the current governor, Francis Nwifuru.

Speaking partly in Pidgin, he said, in effect: "You're busy preparing your son to be governor after Nwifuru. God won't let that happen. You want to use Ebonyi State to settle your child. Let the young man come and meet us on the street so we can teach him how to make 'money na water'."
This is Cubana Chief Priest's claim, and Umahi has not yet responded to this latest attack.
## How it started

The exchange began weeks ago when Cubana Chief Priest described Umahi as the second-worst minister from the South-East. Umahi hit back by telling him he was "becoming very noisy", comparing him unfavourably with Dangote and Otedola, and asking, "How many people have you given scholarships?"
Now the socialite has turned the argument back to politics, questioning what Umahi has done to win South-East votes for the President.
## Over to you
Who is winning this war of words: the minister or the socialite? And is Cubana Chief Priest right to question what the South-East has to show for supporting Tinubu?
more: Cubana Chief Priest nicknamed Umahi 'Pharaoh'.
He accused Umahi of fake promises to Tinubu on South-East votes.

stories.h: Nigeria seeks $500m World Bank loan for infrastructure financing platform
stories.p: The federal government has approached the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into infrastructure, part of a wider $3.85 billion programme called INFRAGROW.
body: The federal government has asked the World Bank for a $500 million loan to set up a platform to attract private investment into Nigerian infrastructure.
## The loan

According to a World Bank project document updated on 4 November 2026 and reported on Monday, 9 November, the facility is part of a broader $3.85 billion programme called the Nigeria Infrastructure Financing and De-Risking Platform for Growth and Jobs, or INFRAGROW. The Federal Ministry of Finance is listed as the borrower and the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (NSIA) as the implementing agency. The aim is to reduce the risks that discourage private investors from funding infrastructure projects.
## Why the bank says it is needed

The World Bank estimates that Nigeria has an infrastructure financing gap of about $100 billion a year, which holds back growth, competitiveness and job creation. It says the problem is not only a lack of money but also weak project preparation and difficulty turning proposals into commercially viable investments.
## Atiku objects

ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar said on Tuesday, 10 November, that the government had no business taking on new debt on its way out. In a statement by his campaign spokesman, he said the World Bank was due to consider the loan on 25 May 2027, four days before the next presidential inauguration, and urged the bank not to approve it on that timetable and to publish its full terms, risks and repayment conditions first. The government has said the platform is needed to attract private investment into infrastructure.
## Background

The request comes as President Bola Tinubu also seeks Senate approval for about $7.7 billion in new external borrowing, and as government borrowing becomes a major campaign issue. NDC candidate Peter Obi has challenged the President to account for loans, while the Presidency says claims that it has borrowed ₦120 trillion are distorted. The World Bank reported last week that Nigeria's total external debt rose to about $145 billion in 2025.
more: The $500m loan is part of a $3.85bn programme.
The NSIA would run the platform.
Borrowing is a major campaign issue.

stories.h: Hamzat vows to enforce one-year rent limit as Lagos governorship candidates debate
stories.p: Lagos APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat says the state will enforce the legal limit on advance rent to one year, warning landlords against demanding two or three years upfront. He spoke at a televised governorship debate.
body: Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for governor, says the state government will enforce the legal limit on advance rent payments.
## What he said

Speaking at a governorship debate organised by a coalition of media organisations on Sunday, 8 November 2026, Hamzat said the one-year cap on advance rent is already contained in the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency law passed in 2025, and that the focus now is making sure it is followed. He warned landlords against demanding two or three years' rent upfront, and said estate agents are required to register with the state and appear on an official database, urging residents to check it before dealing with agents.
## The law

The Lagos State Tenancy Law of 2011 already makes it unlawful for landlords or their agents to demand more than one year's rent in advance from a new tenant, and limits advance payments from sitting tenants. Despite this, demands for two or more years' rent have remained a widespread concern.
## Rhodes-Vivour's pitch

At the same debate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, the governorship candidate of the opposition ADC, said APC governments in Lagos had focused on policies that favoured the elite for more than 20 years, while residents of poorer and rural communities did not feel the benefit of the state's high revenue. He promised more than 100,000 housing units, a safer and cleaner state, and technology-driven measures to end flooding.
## Background

Hamzat is seeking to succeed Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu in the 2027 governorship election. Former governor Akinwunmi Ambode recently pledged to mobilise support for him. Housing costs are one of the biggest concerns for Lagos residents.
more: Hamzat says the one-year rent cap will be enforced.
Estate agents must register with the state.
He spoke at a televised governorship debate.

stories.h: House in Kano State catches fire, blaze linked to solar panel installation
stories.p: A house in Kano State has caught fire, with the blaze linked to its solar power installation. Photos show flames bursting through the roof beside the solar panels as neighbours try to help. The exact cause has not yet been confirmed.
body: A house in Kano State has caught fire, with the incident being linked to its solar power installation.
## Flames on the roof

Photos from the scene show thick smoke rising from the roof of a two-storey building, with flames breaking through beside a row of solar panels. A man can be seen climbing up to an upper-floor balcony as a crowd of neighbours gathers below, some filming on their phones and others watching in shock.
## A growing safety concern
The incident raises serious concerns about the safety of solar installations, especially as more Nigerians turn to solar energy because of unreliable electricity supply.

Poor wiring, faulty batteries, overloaded inverters and improper installation can all create fire hazards. Experts often advise homeowners to use qualified installers, buy certified equipment and have their systems checked regularly.
## Cause not yet confirmed
The exact cause of this particular fire has not yet been independently confirmed.
## Over to you
As more Nigerians embrace solar power, are we paying enough attention to proper installation and safety checks?
more: A house in Kano caught fire near its solar panels.
Faulty wiring, batteries and inverters can all cause fires.
The exact cause has not been confirmed.
